messages:
incident-bot: Pager P1 -> continuous-batcher: high tail latency + node crashes in us-west-2. Triggered at 2026-03-15T09:00:10Z. Service: continuous-batcher, impact: customer-facing latency spikes and 5% request errors.
Maya: oncall here, looking now. any initial telemetry links?
Ravi: https://telemetry.redwood/internal/graph?range=15m&query=batcher_queue_length - queue growing from 200 to ~10k in 7m. Also seeing repeated OOMs on worker-3 and worker-7.
Priya: I'm seeing kernel logs on worker-3:
```
Mar 15 08:59:58 worker-3 kubelet: containerd: runtime error: runtime/cgo: pthread_create failed: Resource temporarily unavailable
Mar 15 08:59:59 worker-3 dockerd: OOMKilled process: continuous-batcher pid=4321
Mar 15 09:00:02 worker-3 nvidia: GPU 0: failed to allocate 1.2GB - CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
```
Jonas: looks like continuous batching is growing batch windows without backpressure. The KV cache is also getting hot which is causing paging to CPU and then container swaps.
Maya: confirmed customers calling in. @sre-lead any SLA concerns?
sre-lead: P1 - potential SLA breach for <customer-acme>. Priority mitigation first, postmortem later.
Maya: immediate mitigation plan: 1) Shift traffic away from us-west-2 to us-east-1 for tolerant routes. 2) Reduce continuous-batcher max_batch_size and disable dynamic growth. 3) Evacuate affected nodes and restart. 4) Engage runtime team for CUDA OOM investigation.
Ravi: starting traffic shift now - updating router policy to prefer us-east-1 for model: text-gen-v2 (non-strict). Patch queued: `route update --from=us-west-2 --to=us-east-1 --selector=model:text-gen-v2 --drain=30s`
runtime-bot: Deployment-Runner: scale-down request accepted for continuous-batcher pool us-west-2 -> reducing replicas from 12 to 4 (graceful).
Priya: disabling continuous batching growth in config on the leader: `CONT_BATCH_GROWTH=off` applying via ssm.
Jonas: I'm tailing logs for batcher: sample: `batcher: queue_size=8123 growth=+1200/s latency_p50=200ms p99=4.2s` then `batcher: critical: spin-lock wait deadlocked` and then `containerd: oom`
Maya: rolling restart nodes worker-3 and worker-7. Ravi, can you mark them as unschedulable?
Ravi: cordon + drain started on worker-3. `kubectl cordon worker-3 && kubectl drain worker-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
Priya: adding temporary queue throttle at the ingress to cap inflight requests per route to 100. Command: `redwoodctl throttle set --route /api/v1/generation --concurrency 100`
Jonas: we need to reduce per-request memory footprint too - switching model instance to 8-bit quantized variant for traffic routed to us-east-1. Doing canary now.
sre-lead: good. update on customer impact: error rate peaked at 5.1% for 12 minutes, median latency for affected routes jumped from 120ms to 1.8s, top customers hit: acme, betaapp. Notify CS.
Maya: @Priya please draft incident notice for CS and send to the affected customers, include mitigation and ETA (90m).
Priya: drafting now. sending to #customer-notify in 10m.
Ravi: worker-7 shows repeated CUDA panics in dmesg: `nvidia: scheduling barrier exceeded, blocking for 200ms` followed by `segfault` in the runtime process. Pushing logs to /tmp/incident-2276543210/worker-7.log
Jonas: suggestion: disable KV persistence to prevent heavy disk paging while we stabilize. Set `KV_CACHE_PERSIST=false` on the leader node.
Maya: accepted. Priya, do that as well as post a note in the incident doc.
Priya: done: KV persistence off and posted note at https://confluence.redwood/incidents/2276543210
runtime-bot: Runtime team assigned: @Jonas, @Ravi. Escalation to Runtime SRE requested.
Jonas: running diagnostic script across batcher pods: `scripts/diag-batcher.sh --collect core,gpu,heap --out /tmp/diag-2276.tar.gz`
Ravi: core dumps indicate repeated memory fragmentation then sudden spike -> OOM -> container killed. Suspect a leak in the continuous batching path when queue growth crosses threshold.
Maya: do we have a rollback that stops continuous-batcher feature entirely?
Jonas: yes, feature-flag off `feature.continuous_batching=false` in cluster config. Rolling to 100% in us-west-2 now.
incident-bot: Feature flag update recorded: continuous_batching disabled at 2026-03-15T09:12:45Z by Jonas.
Maya: after disabling, queue started draining. p99 latency down to 420ms within 6 minutes. Error rate dropping.
Priya: customers notified. CS confirmed first responses sent to acme and betaapp.
sre-lead: good containment. keep an eye for node flaps post-restart. set follow-up: rollback if any further OOMs.
Ravi: worker-9 now showing high system swap usage, suspect some kernel panics during earlier paging. Initiating full node reboot and kernel dmesg capture.
Jonas: recommended long-term: add backpressure in the batch growth algorithm (cap growth per second) and add a circuit-breaker that rejects new batch growth when GPU memory usage > 80%. Also add async KV eviction with LRU TTL to avoid persistent paging.
Maya: assign follow-ups: [Ravi] collect core dumps + GPU logs and attach to ticket INC-2276543210; [Jonas] implement quick patch for growth cap and circuit-breaker; [Priya] customer comms + postmortem. Deadline: initial RCA draft in 72h.
Priya: created ticket INC-2276543210 and assigned. Posting link to incident doc now.
Ravi: uploading artifacts (core dumps, gpu logs) to secure bucket: s3://incidents/2276543210/artifacts
Jonas: local repro attempt: running loadtest + continuous growth patch in staging reproduced queue growth and deadlock within 3 minutes. Patch seems to prevent runaway. Will PR tonight.
Maya: monitoring... us-west-2 p99 now 310ms, error rate 0.6%. Looks stable for 20m.
sre-lead: +1 for closing pager if stable for 30m. keep incident channel for postmortem notes.
incident-bot: Pager auto-close scheduled in 30m if all alerts clear.
Maya: thanks all. great coordination.
Priya: filing final customer follow-up template and scheduling postmortem meeting.
